report_text:
IMPLEMENTER_REPORT:
ROUND: 0
STATUS: DONE
SUGGESTION_RESOLUTIONS:
none
SELF_REVIEW:
- Found: `ExpectedSetEntry::resolution` was the last entry-level failure vocabulary; `generate_manifest` still gated on it, so a directory-resolved entry whose root `SKILL.md` was missing could still invent a manifest entry → fixed by deriving failure from `ExpectedSetEntry::is_failed()` (owned skill files) and deleting the field.
- Found: stale prose in `CONTEXT.md` said an entry carries "whether that location was resolved" → fixed to the file-level terminology; ADR-0045 already recorded the retirement, so no ADR edit was needed.
- Found: three skill-index tests and one validation-runner fixture read the retired field; migrated them to the root `SkillFile` resolution (same assertion strength, plus `is_failed()` on failed-entry tests), dropped the `resolution` initializer from the shared `entry()` helper, and renamed `expected_set_entries_carry_resolved_dirs_and_status` → `..._and_skill_files`.
- No issues: no consumer outside `skill-index` read the entry-level field (`crates/deploy/src/dev.rs`, `crates/deploy/src/pack.rs`, `crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs`, `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs` all read `file.resolution` only).
- No issues: formatting of both edited Rust files is rustfmt-clean; repo-wide `cargo fmt --check` has 70 pre-existing diffs in untouched files (e.g. `crates/deploy/src/distill.rs`), left alone.
CHANGED_FILES:
- crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs (edited: removed `ExpectedSetEntry::resolution` and its doc; updated `ResolutionStatus` docs to describe a Skill file; `generate_manifest` now skips failed entries via `is_failed()`; migrated 4 test assertions/initializers; added RED→GREEN test `generate_manifest_derives_failure_from_owned_skill_files`)
- crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs (edited: test fixture `test_entry` no longer initializes the retired field; no production change)
- CONTEXT.md (edited: "Expected-set entry" term now says the entry carries the Skill files it owns and has no directory-level resolution state)
- crates/deploy/src/dev.rs (pre-existing — file-level failure landed in #124; unchanged here)
- crates/deploy/src/pack.rs (pre-existing — file-level failure landed in #124; unchanged here)
- tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs (pre-existing — migrated onto skill files in #125; unchanged here)
- docs/adr/0045-expected-set-entry-resolves-its-skill-files.md (pre-existing — already records the retirement as decision/consequence; unchanged here)
- corpus/issue-126.json (pre-existing — ticket spec; read only)
- corpus/issue-121.json (pre-existing — parent spec; read only)
- TASK.md (pre-existing — task contract at `../TASK.md`; read only)
- IMPLEMENTER_REPORT.md (new — this report)
SUMMARY: Retired the entry-level resolution status, making the owned Skill files the single failure vocabulary while keeping every dev/pack/validation message and behavior intact.

## Acceptance criteria → executed evidence

AC1 — entry no longer exposes a directory-level resolution status or its reason strings; failure derived from skill files.
- `ExpectedSetEntry` in `crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs:70-92` now has `skill_files: Vec<SkillFile>` and no `resolution` field; `is_failed()` (line 93) is `any(file.resolution is Missing)`. `ResolutionStatus` docs (lines 25-35) now describe one Skill file, not a source directory.
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets` — EXIT 0, so nothing in the workspace reads the removed field.
- `grep -rn "\.resolution" crates/*/src tests` — remaining hits are `file.resolution` / `t.file.resolution` only (`crates/deploy/src/pack.rs:179`, `crates/deploy/src/dev.rs:61`, `crates/validation-runner/src/lib.rs:136,1174`, `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs:66`); `grep -rn "entry\.resolution\|\.resolution:"` outside `skill-index` — no hits.
- RED→GREEN test: `cargo test -p skill-index generate_manifest_derives_failure_from_owned_skill_files` failed before the fix (`crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs:1074`, "an entry owning a missing skill file must not invent a manifest entry") and passes after.

AC2 — dev/pack/validation failure messages keep naming the missing location and reason.
- No consumer message code was touched (`dev.rs`, `pack.rs`, `validation-runner` failure paths read `SkillFile::resolution`), so wording is unchanged from #124/#123.
- Executed dev capture (`cargo test -p deploy dev_warns_and_skips_an_entry_with_a_missing_skill_file -- --nocapture`): `WARNING: autopilot skill 'alpha' is missing skill files, skipping: skill file not found: .../skills/autopilot/alpha/SKILL.md`; vendor/upstream variants likewise name their directory.
- Pack: `cargo test -p deploy pack_fails_when_a_skill_directory_lacks_its_root_skill_md` — PASS (asserts the error names the skill and `SKILL.md`, no tarball produced); `pack_fails_on_missing_vendor_entry` — PASS.
- Validation: `cargo test -p validation-runner matrix_missing_directory_fails_for_lock_driven_sources` — 1 passed; `cargo test -p validation-runner matrix_missing_skill_md_fails_for_every_source` — 1 passed (each asserts the report names the missing directory/file per source); `validate_all` still embeds the enumerator's `reason` for a missing file.

AC3 — repo compiles, `cargo test --workspace` green, no consumer reads the retired status, clippy clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` — EXIT 0 (one full green run; every target `ok`).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — EXIT 0 (only the two pre-existing cargo unused-dependency warnings for `anyhow` and `serde_json` in `crates/validation/Cargo.toml:7,9`).
- Consumer grep above: no entry-level reader remains.

AC4 — behavior unchanged vs the previous ticket (dev policy, pack strictness, tarball/installed layout, lock format, entry-state verdicts).
- `crates/deploy`, `crates/validation-runner`, `tests/test_install.rs` (7 passed), `tests/test_build.rs` (1 passed), `tests/test_toolkit_setup.rs` (1 passed) all green with no consumer code changed.
- Deliberate change (per AC1): entry-level `resolution` and its reason strings leave the interface.
- Derived, disclosed: `generate_manifest` now skips entries whose source directory resolved but an owned skill file is missing (previously they were listed). In the shipped `pack` path this is unreachable — `reject_failed_entries` (`crates/deploy/src/pack.rs:172-201`) bails before manifest generation — so tarball/installed output is unchanged. This is the direct consequence of "failure is derived from the skill files the entry owns".

AC5 — existing suites referee, green without relaxing any assertion.
- Migrated assertions are the same property at the same seam: `alpha.skill_file(None).unwrap().resolution == Resolved` replaces `alpha.resolution == Resolved` (and likewise `show_me`, `tdd`), and the failed-entry tests assert the root file's `Missing { reason }` plus `is_failed()`, which is *more* specific than the retired field.
- `cargo test -p skill-index -p validation-runner -p deploy` — 35 + 22 + 34 passed, 0 failed.
- Full workspace suite green; integration suites green.

Test-status note (honesty): in 4 full `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` runs, one run failed `distill-cli`'s `transition::tests::commit_writes_run_artifact_with_exact_bytes` with `commit succeeds: "injected state write failure for run-1"`. This is a pre-existing in-process env race: `crates/distill-cli/src/transition.rs:272` sets `DISTILL_FAIL_WRITE_STATE_FOR_RUN=run-1` while the sibling test at `transition.rs:230` also uses `run-1`; it passes alone (3/3 reruns) and the suite reran green. Not caused by or related to T126 (files untouched). Baseline likewise had an intermittent `shared::tests::project_root_finds_real_root` failure during parallel runs.

## TDD evidence

RED — production change came after a failing test.
- Added `generate_manifest_derives_failure_from_owned_skill_files` in `crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs` (fixture: `skills/autopilot/broken/reasonix/SKILL.md` present, root `SKILL.md` absent).
- Command: `cargo test -p skill-index generate_manifest_derives_failure_from_owned_skill_files`
- Result: FAILED — `panicked at crates/skill-index/src/lib.rs:1074: an entry owning a missing skill file must not invent a manifest entry`.
- Reason for RED: `generate_manifest` gated on `matches!(skill.resolution, ResolutionStatus::Resolved)`, and the directory-resolved entry therefore produced a manifest entry.

GREEN — after deleting the field and gating on `skill.is_failed()`.
- `cargo test -p skill-index` — 22 passed, 0 failed (includes the new test).
- `cargo test -p skill-index -p validation-runner -p deploy` — 35 + 22 + 34 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` — EXIT 0.

REFACTOR — no behavior-bearing refactor: doc comments updated, test fixture initializer removed, `rustfmt --check` clean on both edited files, clippy `-D warnings` clean.

## Clause checks
